svg.title: macOS · Import from Device · project list · 460×520
svg.desc: Mirrors Remote/ImportWindow.swift (selectingProject phase) over Shared/ProjectTransferProtocol.swift (PTListReply / PTProjectInfo). One row per project on the paired device, newest first, as the serving side ordered them. The list is ALWAYS answered whatever that device is doing — it is kilobytes, and a client that cannot see the list has no idea why it cannot; it is `requestTransfer` that gets refused, with the reason as a sentence ("That device is shooting right now.") rather than a bare "busy". The reply is re-walked on every request rather than served from an arm-time cache: a shoot finished since the code was minted is exactly the project somebody is here to fetch. The byte figure is the project folder's true, uncompressed size — the payload path is file-by-file with no compression, so this is also exactly what will cross the wire, which is why the progress bar downstream needs no "about". Thumbnails do NOT travel with this list. They used to, and on a real library that was wrong twice over: the whole catalogue is one control frame, so images had to share a budget; and the serving device only holds a cached tile for assets some grid has actually drawn, so most rows arrived blank anyway (measured on a 293-project phone: 62 of 293). Each row now asks for its own tile as it appears (`requestThumbnail` → `PTThumbnailReply`), and the serving device GENERATES one if the cache has none — a full RAW decode for a DNG, which is unthinkable for a whole catalogue and exactly the bargain the local Gallery already makes for the handful of rows on screen. The result is persisted under the same cache key the local grids read, so the second look is free and those grids get it for nothing too. Measured on this Mac (2026-08-28): 79 of 79 rows drawn, 1.5 MB of tiles, 10.3 s on the first pass and instant on the second. A row whose project has no drawable source keeps the placeholder (row 3) and is not asked for again. A HIDE IMPORTED checkbox heads the list, ticked by default (2026-09-06): a device you pull from regularly answers with its whole library every time, and after the first session most of it is already here. What it hides is AppModel.hasImported(originID:) — the same test the .lapse door uses, matching a remote captureID against both the ids here and the origins recorded on projects imported earlier, so it catches a project pulled FROM that device AND one that started here and was sent TO it. Projects imported before importedFromID was recorded have no thread back and read as not-imported, which is the honest answer. The header still counts the WHOLE library the device offered (4) while the list draws what survived the filter (3); unticking brings the hidden rows back, each marked "Already in your library" in accent, and re-ticking drops them from the selection so the footer cannot cost bytes for a row nobody can see. When everything on that device is already here the list is replaced outright by a centred "Already in your library / All N projects on that device have been imported. Untick “Hide imported” to see them." — an empty list under a ticked box would read as a broken link. Selecting a row arms the Import button; the footer states what the pull will cost before it starts. A SELECT pop-up sits at the trailing end of the Hide imported band (2026-09-18): Custom — the resting state, rows picked by hand — Today, Yesterday, This Week and All. A bucket REPLACES the selection with the matching VISIBLE rows in list order (the pulls run in it), so the batch can still be trimmed or grown before Import; the buckets are the shoot's createdAt in THIS device's calendar — today is today here, not on the phone; the week is the locale's, not a rolling seven days; Yesterday is that day alone — and a date bucket is offered only while it would pick at least one visible row ("Today" with every today's shoot already imported is exactly the no-op item this avoids), so the menu can be as short as Custom · All. Any hand change — a row tap, a Hide imported toggle, Back — returns it to Custom; it is disabled when nothing is visible. The pop-up is a SIBLING of the checkbox's button, never inside its label, so it owns its own clicks; the checkbox keeps everything left of the "Select:" label as its hit area. Small control size: an 11 pt band, and the regular pop-up reads heavy. Staged without a peer by LL_TRANSFER_LIST=1 (nine rows across today / yesterday / this week / older, two wearing this library's own origin ids) and =old (every row a week back, so the menu prunes to Custom · All); verified 2026-09-18 on this Mac through accessibility, every bucket and every return to Custom. EMPTY LIBRARY (desc-only): "No projects on that device / Nothing to import yet." Verified 2026-08-27 end to end against a simulator serving its library.
svg.text: macOS · Import from Device · project list · 460×520 pt window
mirrors Remote/ImportWindow.swift over PTListReply — Hide imported on · Select: Custom · all-hidden and empty-library states desc-only
